response.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt,
        AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_iga_minus_igm
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
with_overall_mean AS (
    SELECT
        ID,
        SEX,
        avg_pt,
        avg_iga_minus_igm,
        AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) OVER () AS overall_mean
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT
    SEX,
    AVG(avg_pt) AS average_patient_avg_pt,
    AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) AS average_patient_avg_iga_minus_igm,
    AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm / overall_mean) AS average_ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM with_overall_mean
GROUP BY SEX
ORDER BY SEX;

assumptions.assumption: Patients are included when they have at least one matching laboratory record; SQL AVG ignores NULL PT and ignores a record's IGA−IGM difference when either value is NULL. The overall mean is across patients with a non-NULL IGA−IGM average.
A NULL SEX is grouped separately from the empty-string SEX group, as SQL GROUP BY treats NULL as its own group.
